audit.why: 40.59% Emerald+ and 7/10 HARD is right. She has a level-1, point-and-click follow-up CC in Permafrost, and Kassadin has no escape until 6. What the page frames well is that this is a hard lane rather than a hard matchup — she is a tank, so nothing she does after two items scales.

audit.whatIsWrong: win[4] (Level 6) said Sejuani under a caption that reads 'dragging you from helpless toward even — skill decides how clean the escape is', and win[6] (Two+ items) said Sejuani under a caption that reads 'you blink past Permafrost and burst her squishies, and as a tank she has no scaling to reclaim it'. full.phases[4] and [6] repeated the mismatch.
audit.why: A caption that says 'toward even, skill decides' is the definition of Skill, and a caption that says she cannot reclaim it is a Kassadin win. The First item stage was already Skill and stays there.
audit.corrected: Level 6 to Skill and Two+ items to Kassadin on win[] and phases[].side. The four early stages stay Sejuani.

audit.whatIsWrong: Sejuani's passive is never mentioned on either layer, and it contains the two facts that decide the matchup. Riot's Fury of the North text: 'After being out of combat, Sejuani gains Frost Armor which grants Armor and Magic Resist and immunity to slows. Frost Armor persists for a short time after Sejuani takes damage. Sejuani can damage a stunned enemy to shatter it, dealing massive magic damage.' First: she is immune to slows while Frost Armor holds, so Force Pulse — Kassadin's only disengage tool other than the blink — does nothing to her opening walk-up. Second: a Permafrost stun is not just lost time, it is the setup for a shatter that deals massive magic damage, which is why eating one is usually the whole death.
audit.why: Both clauses are verbatim in Riot's passive description, and both change how you play the lane: you stop trying to kite her with E, and you treat the stun as a burst rather than a CC.
audit.corrected: Slow immunity is now stated in mid, whys[4], wants.you[2], tradeGood, breakdown.cooldowns and loading; the shatter is in mid, spikes[3], wants.foe[1] and enemyWin.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two problems. dosFull[2].d offered a 'fifteen-second invitation' after Arctic Assault, and the full layer builds every green light on 'wait for Permafrost' style advice without numbers.
audit.why: Arctic Assault is 18/16.5/15/13.5/12s — eighteen at rank 1, not fifteen. Permafrost is a 1.5-second cooldown, so waiting for it to come off cooldown is not a plan at all; what gates it is whether you are carrying maximum Frost stacks. Those are opposite kinds of clock and the page treated them the same.
audit.corrected: Arctic Assault's 18s is now stated in winCon, spikes[1], dosFull[0], dosFull[2], breakdown.cooldowns, report[5] and loading, and Permafrost is explicitly called a 1.5s cooldown you avoid by stack management rather than by counting.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.late claims 'Q-silence the counterplay'; several full-layer fields call Sejuani 'him'.
audit.why: Null Sphere does not silence — Riot's text is 'dealing damage and interrupting channels'. Sejuani is female.
audit.corrected: Silence replaced with the interrupt; pronouns fixed inside the strings I rewrote.

edits.before: Nether Blade's quintupled mana restore on champion hits lets you farm under tower without going dry, and a maxed Null Sphere shield blunts a little of her burst — but this is survival, not a fight window. Respect Arctic Assault: if she charges in, your Q shield only soaks magic, so blink or sidestep the engage rather than tank the stun. At 6, Riftwalk is your exhale — blink to safety the instant she or her jungler tries to chain CC you, and use it to dodge the Arctic Assault into Permafrost setup. You are clawing toward even, not winning.
edits.after: Nether Blade's quintupled mana restore on champion hits lets you farm under tower without going dry, and a maxed Null Sphere shield blunts a little of her burst — but this is survival, not a fight window. notes: Left alone deliberately: five fields (early, whys[1], whys[3], spikes[0], wants.you[1]) say Winter's Wrath 'slams a percent of your max HP'. Riot's DDragon text for Winter's Wrath is only 'swings her mace twice, dealing damage, slowing enemies and applying Frost stacks' and sejuani.json carries no percentHealth flag on W — but absence in the kit file means unknown, not false, so I did not touch those lines. Someone with the live tooltip should confirm or kill the max-HP wording. Same for 'each auto feeds a Frost stack': Riot's text attributes Frost stacks to W only and says nothing about basic attacks. Kit-flag misfire as elsewhere: _missing-interactions.json says 'Sejuani can cancel your Null Sphere (Q) with Fury of the North (P), Permafrost (E), Glacial Prison (R)', built on a bad channel flag on Null Sphere. Riot's description says Null Sphere interrupts channels rather than being one, so that row is not on the page.
